title: Arriving in New Orleans and living on Bourbon Street
summary: Kelly drives to New Orleans with the Nurse brothers and shares a room with drummer Johnny Grant.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You have to be careful. Now you were talking about Leslie Nurse, was his name?

Yeah. Leslie and Bill Nurse were two brothers. One played piano and one played banjo. They had a little band in the street, but their parents had moved to New Orleans. My father was a Presbyterian minister, and so Leslie and I drove down to New Orleans, and Johnny Grant, who was a drummer from Straitford, had a room at 327 Bourbon Street. It was a rooming house. He offered me an opportunity to stay with him. I didn't have to pay any of that. I landed in New Orleans for eight dollars, and I planned that in the Satchelor in the province of the Johnwood, where I went. And so, Johnny was in, though. He'd been playing with other bands all around town.
That's with the Owls at one time, I remember. Sure.
